NoteTexAccessor::strip_graphics¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteTexAccessor::strip_graphics() const

Remove Direct Graphics And Figure Containers¶

strip_graphics() removes complete \includegraphics calls and complete figure or figure* environments. It is the broad image cleanup operation: direct inclusions disappear wherever they occur, and a figure container is removed with its caption, labels, and body. Use strip_figs() when standalone graphic calls must survive, or graphics_tags() when a graphic call should become an explicit text marker rather than disappear.

An \includegraphics call may have one balanced optional group followed by one balanced required path group. Nested braces in either group are respected. The command is removed only when the complete required group exists. Figure regions are same-name depth balanced and starred names are handled separately. Escaped commands, longer control words, incomplete calls, and unclosed figure regions remain unchanged.

Removal is cell-local, out-of-place, and shape preserving. ASCII whitespace is collapsed and cells are trimmed; a cell containing only a graphic becomes an empty string, not an absent cell. Undefined input propagates and defined non-Text Notes reject. Runtime is linear in source bytes and does not access the filesystem or decode image content.

Example 1: Options, Nested Paths, Figures, And Malformed Calls¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(A \includegraphics[width={0.5\textwidth}]{img/{plot}.pdf} B)",
    R"(C \begin{figure}body\end{figure} D \begin{figure*}wide\end{figure*} E)",
    R"(\\includegraphics{escaped} \includegraphics{unfinished)"});
std::cout << source.tex().strip_graphics() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["A B", "C D E", "\\\\includegraphics{escaped} \\includegraphics{unfinished"]

Example 2: Empty Cells Retain Matrix Position¶

const auto grid = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(\includegraphics{a})", "plain",
                             R"(\begin{figure}b\end{figure})", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto clean = grid.tex().strip_graphics();
std::cout << clean << '\n';
std::cout << "shape=[" << clean.size(0) << ", " << clean.size(1) << "]\n";
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "idempotent=" << ((clean == clean.tex().strip_graphics()).all().bool_item())
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["", "plain"], 
  ["", ""]
]
shape=[2, 2]
idempotent=true

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Dtype¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().strip_graphics().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().strip_graphics();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "strip graphics Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
strip graphics Int64: rejected

See Also¶
